thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — high 5xx rate for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (automated detection). Alert severity: HIGH. Paging on-call.

maria_g: acked, jumping in. seeing ~25% errors, latency spike to 2.1s p95.

devon_s: on it — I'm pulling routing metrics and smart-routing decision logs.

sre_lead: quick checklist: (1) scope customers impacted (2) confirm whether fallbacks triggered (3) validate DNS/edge.

maria_g: customer-impact quick note: traffic to hosted-api eu region. Some requests routed to a model variant tagged `gptt-2-small` which we decommissioned last week — that could explain validation errors.

eng_prod: wait, why would smart-routing pick `gptt-2-small`? policy should prefer matching model-tag then fallback to nearest region. Did a policy change go out?

devon_s: pulling policy history... found a config push 45m ago that updated fallback chain for eu -> global -> us-east. looks normal. but routing logs show requests for eu being resolved to endpoint eu-edge-old.rwd.ai (decom) 

maria_g: DNS check from a few edge nodes: `dig +short eu.service.rwd.ai` -> returns CNAME to `eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` for some resolvers, `eu-edge-new.rwd.ai` for others. inconsistent. TTLs on the old records were 1h.

ops_bot: system note: CDN invalidation completed 2h ago for eu-edge-new, but DNS change didn't propagate fully — looks like resolver caches holding old CNAME.

sre_lead: hmm that explains routing loop: old edge is returning a healthy route but it's connected to retired compute pools referencing the old model variant. Smart-routing sees endpoint up -> routes -> inference fails -> fallback triggers -> routes again -> oscillation.

devon_s: logs snippet: ```
[router] decision: prefer eu-edge-old.rwd.ai -> send to host 10.12.3.45
[host] model-check: variant gptt-2-small not available -> error 422
[router] fallback: route -> global-edge-1 -> global-edge-1 resolves back to eu-edge-old via DNS
```

maria_g: mitigation plan step 1: prevent routing loops by temporarily locking fallback policy to prefer-primary-region and disable circular fallback for eu for next 30m. Can someone apply?

eng_prod: I'm applying the policy lock now via console and CLI. `redwoodctl routing set-policy eu --fallback-policy prefer-primary --disable-circular-true --note "incident 1782102468"`

eng_prod: done. policy change rolled out to routers (prop 1).

sre_lead: step 2: reduce DNS TTLs to 30s and force purge old CNAMEs from known public resolvers where possible. ops, can you coordinate with CDN/DNS provider?

ops_bot: contacting provider support (ticket #CDN-58421). Meanwhile forcing purge on CloudEdge: `cloudedge purge eu-edge-old.rwd.ai` -> response: queued.

devon_s: writing a query to count affected requests by origin resolver: `select count(*) from router_logs where region='eu' and upstream_host='eu-edge-old.rwd.ai' and status>=500 since -60m` -> ~43k requests. Error rate ~22% overall for region.

maria_g: customer impact estimate: ~3.5% of total hosted API customers saw increased error rates for ~46 minutes. Noting a few high-volume customers reported 5xx spikes.

sre_lead: good. step 3 rollback: point any smart-routing entries referencing `eu-edge-old` to `eu-edge-new` immediately. eng_prod, can you push a route override?

eng_prod: pushing route override: `redwoodctl routing override set --host eu-edge-old.rwd.ai --target eu-edge-new.rwd.ai --ttl 60` -> rolled to all routing proxies.

maria_g: verifying with `curl -v https://eu.service.rwd.ai/health` from multiple nodes — now resolves to eu-edge-new for 9/10 nodes, last one still showing old -> waiting for purge.

devon_s: also noticed in traces that fallback policy was mis-evaluating model-variant compatibility because of a mapping file `/etc/redwood/model_variant_map.json` on the old pool that included `gptt-2-small`. That file should have been removed during decommission.

sre_lead: assign owner to clean decommission artifacts: tim_k take point with infra to ensure no stray mapping files remain on retired pools.

tim_k: on it — kicking a job to sweep retired pools. `infra-cleanup --tag retired --check model_variant_map.json` -> queued.

ops_bot: CDN purge completed for most POPs. provider reports positive propagation but some ISP caches still stubborn.

maria_g: continuing monitoring. error rate trending down — now 7% and falling. p95 latency back to 450ms.

devon_s: while we recover, recommend we keep the fallback lock for +30m and leave override in place for +60m. Also drop DNS TTL change to 15s if still flapping.

sre_lead: agreed. extended locks applied. also opening an RCA ticket and a customer-impact tracker. please add any customers that submitted support tickets.

eng_prod: adding quick mitigation note to status page: "Partial degradation for EU-hosted inference endpoints; mitigation in progress. No data loss; temporary routing policy enforced." :warning:

maria_g: handoff to next on-call in 30 minutes. summary for oncall-next: root cause is stale DNS/CNAME pointing some resolvers to decommissioned edge which had leftover model variant mapping producing validation errors, creating fallback oscillation. Mitigations applied: routing fallback lock, route override to eu-edge-new, CDN purge, infra sweep for mapping artifacts.

oncall-next: reading and acking. will monitor for the next 2 hours and coordinate with support for customer follow-ups.

sre_lead: timeline note (for postmortem): first alert at 1782102468, policy change/override at 1782102760, CDN purge effective 1782103380, rolling recovery starting 1782103600, incident declared resolved for customers at 1782106000 but monitoring will continue.

maria_g: closing slack updates — will paste postmortem link once created. great job team :thumbsup:
